subject: math
title: Multi-Digit Multiplication
seo_title: Grade 4 Multi-Digit Multiplication Worksheets: Area Model, Partial Products and Standard Algorithm
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
standard_text: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 multiplication worksheets: area models and partial products, the standard algorithm for 3- and 4-digit × 1-digit and 2-digit × 2-digit numbers, word problems and estimating to check. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Break the numbers apart by place value. Multiply each part, then add.
key_sub: 47 × 6 = 240 + 42 = 282. For 2-digit × 2-digit there are 4 partial products, and the second row of the standard algorithm starts with a 0 because it multiplies by tens.
body_html:
Break the number apart by place value

A big multiplication is a few small ones. Split each number into tens and ones (or thousands, hundreds, tens and ones). Multiply each part, then add the partial products.

The standard algorithm

Write the numbers in columns and start with the ones. When a product is 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup the rest to the next column. Multiply first, then add the regrouped digit.

Two-digit × two-digit: 4 partial products

Each part of one number multiplies each part of the other. Two parts × two parts = 4 partial products.

Standard algorithm

34 × 27 = ?

Step 1: 34 × 7 = 238. Step 2: 34 × 20 = 680. Write a 0 in the ones place first, then 34 × 2 = 68. Step 3: 238 + 680 = 918.

Answer: 918

Check with an estimate

Round, multiply in your head, and compare. 34 × 27 is about 30 × 30 = 900, so 918 makes sense. An answer like 306 or 9,180 would be far off.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the regrouped digit (47 × 6 = 242)Write the small digit above the next column and add it
Adding the regrouped digit first (47 × 6 = 482)Multiply first: 4 × 6 = 24, then add 4: 28
No zero in the second row (34 × 27 = 306)The 2 means 20. Write 0 in the ones place, then multiply
Only 2 partial products (34 × 27 = 600 + 28)Multiply every part by every part: 4 partial products
Treating 40 as 4 (47 × 6 = 24 + 42)40 × 6 = 240, not 24

faq.q: How do you teach multi-digit multiplication in 4th grade?
faq.a: Start with the area model or partial products, so children see that 47 × 6 is 40 × 6 plus 7 × 6. Then move to the standard algorithm, which is a short way to write the same partial products.

faq.q: Why do you put a zero in the second row when multiplying 2-digit numbers?
faq.a: In 34 × 27, the 2 means 2 tens, so the second row is 34 × 20, not 34 × 2. The zero in the ones place shows that this row counts tens: 680, not 68.

faq.q: What is an area model for multiplication?
faq.a: It is a rectangle split by place value. For 34 × 27, the sides are 30 + 4 and 20 + 7, so there are 4 parts: 600, 80, 210 and 28. Their sum, 918, is the product.

It is the Common Core Grade 4 standard for multiplying up to a four-digit number by a one-digit number, and a two-digit number by a two-digit number, using place value strategies and explaining the work with equations, arrays or area models.
